title: Formal glueing: Can is an equivalence of R-modules with glueing data
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$, and let $\mathrm{Glue}=\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ be the category of glueing data, with the canonical maps $c^P_f:(P\otimes_RS)_f\to P_f\otimes_RS$ and $\sigma^P_{f,g}:(P_f)_g\to(P_g)_f$ and the localizations $P_f$, $h_f$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. For an $R$-module $M$ put $\mathrm{Can}(M)=(M\otimes_RS,(M_{f_i})_i,(c^M_{f_i})_i,(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$, and for an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ put $\mathrm{Can}(u)=(u\otimes_RS,(u_{f_i})_i)$ [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].
(1) For every $R$-module $P$ and $f,g\in R$ the maps $c^P_f$ and $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ are isomorphisms; $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$, $\mathrm{Can}(u)$ is a morphism $\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$, and $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}$ is a functor.
(2) Assume moreover that $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that, for the ideal $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$, the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Then $\mathrm{Can}$ is an equivalence of categories: it is fully faithful (for $R$-modules $M,N$, every morphism $\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ in $\mathrm{Glue}$ equals $\mathrm{Can}(u)$ for exactly one $R$-linear $u:M\to N$) and essentially surjective (every object of $\mathrm{Glue}$ is isomorphic in $\mathrm{Glue}$ to $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for some $R$-module $M$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813) and its proof (via Lemmas 05EK, 05EP, 05EQ, 05EI); part (1) is the definition of the functor Can in Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data, line 24641), where c and sigma are called the canonical isomorphisms can_i, can_ij. Stacks states (2) as: Can and H^0 are quasi-inverse equivalences; only the equivalence property of Can is stated here
